name: io.github.durenzidu/powpow-mcp
title: PowPow
description: PowPow social MCP: create posts, discover places and people, chat with digital humans.

tools.name: find_nearby
tools.description: Find publicly discoverable digital humans, real users and posts near a place. Results include approximate or exact location (depending on whether the other side enabled precise discovery), type and a summary. This is the core tool for "who is around X" and "what is near X"; calling it renders the public digital humans nearby as the "PowPow Nearby Discovery" card. **You must confirm the place with the user first** — if they say "near me", ask which city, district or landmark; never guess coordinates. For attractions and business districts nearby, call nearby_attractions as well — the two tools together cover the full map-discovery view.

place.description: Place to search, e.g. "Guomao", "Zhongguancun", "Forbidden City". When the user says "near me", ask which place first

types.description: Object types to return: digital_humans / users / posts. All by default

tools.name: geocode_place
tools.description: Resolve a place name or landmark into latitude/longitude for use with find_nearby. Returns matched_name (the POI name actually matched by the geocoder) and confidence (0-1 match score). When a name is ambiguous, check that matched_name is really the place the user means; if unsure, tell the user both and confirm.

tools.name: get_digital_human
tools.description: Get the full profile of one public digital human: persona, bio, avatar, location and current mood. This is the follow-up step after find_nearby returns a digital human — introduce it to the user, then let them talk to it.

id.description: Digital human id (from find_nearby or another tool's result)

tools.name: get_post_detail
tools.description: Get the full text, author, location and engagement counts of one public post, plus the latest 3 comments as an overview (public posts only). For the full discussion, who replied to whom, or replying to a specific person, use get_post_replies — that is the dedicated comment entry point.

post_id.description: Post id. The 8-character short id from search results is enough; a full id or a post link also works

tools.name: get_post_replies
tools.description: Get comments under one public post: top-level comments paginated newest-first, each with its nested replies, author nickname, timestamp and comment id. Use this to see what a post is discussing or to reply to a specific comment (pass reply_to_comment_id using the id returned here). For the post body alone use get_post_detail.

post_id.description: Post id. The 8-character short id from search_posts / my_posts is enough; a link also works

tools.name: nearby_attractions
tools.description: Find attractions and business districts near a place, complementing nearby digital humans to form the full map-discovery capability. Returns two groups — attractions and business_districts — each with distance. Calling it renders them as the "PowPow Nearby Discovery" card. **You must confirm the place with the user first** — if they say "near me", ask which city or district; never guess coordinates.

place.description: Place to search, e.g. "Guomao", "West Lake". When the user says "near me", ask which place first

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: List all public PowPow campaigns (for example the "100 museums in Beijing" check-in campaign), each with its nested check-in spots (acts). Use this to tell the user which activities they can join right now. Calling it renders campaigns as the "PowPow Nearby Discovery" card.

tools.name: search_posts
tools.description: Search public posts by time range and/or keyword. ① Time only (since_hours, or since/until): returns that window as a reverse-chronological feed — use it for "what is new", "what is the community talking about today", "what was posted on 25 October". ② With keyword: ranks posts inside the window by keyword hits, most relevant first. ③ Neither time nor keyword: returns the 20 newest posts site-wide. Time parameters: since_hours=24 means the past 24 hours relative to now; since/until are YYYY-MM-DD Beijing calendar days, until is inclusive. Every result carries its real publish time — judge freshness from it and never assume the results are recent; if the window is empty, say so honestly. Difference from find_nearby: this tool searches by time and keyword across the whole site, find_nearby searches by place.

keyword.description: Keyword matched against post bodies. Omit to get the feed in reverse chronological order.

since.description: Start time, inclusive. A bare date (YYYY-MM-DD) means 00:00 Beijing time that day; a full ISO timestamp with offset also works, e.g. 2026-10-25T08:00:00+08:00.

until.description: End time. A bare date includes the whole day, e.g. until=2026-10-25 means up to 24:00 on the 25th.

since_hours.description: Hours to look back from now, e.g. 24 means the past 24 hours. Use either this or since; when both are given this one wins.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Confirm which PowPow account is currently connected. Returns identity only (user id, username, nickname). Call it when the user asks "who am I", "am I logged in" or "which account is this", and before any action that needs an identity. For account statistics (membership, badge balance, post count, digital human count) use get_my_account instead.

tools.name: get_my_account
tools.description: Overview of the connected account: nickname, badge balance, membership tier and expiry, published post count, digital human count, join date and profile link. Use it for "how many badges do I have", "when does my membership expire", "how many posts have I published". Difference from whoami: whoami answers "who am I"; this tool answers "what state is my account in".

tools.name: my_posts
tools.description: List posts published by the connected account on PowPow, newest first, with location, like/comment counts and original link. Use it for "what have I posted" or "show me my last travel note", and after publishing to confirm the post really went live.

tools.name: get_my_post_replies
tools.description: See replies directed at me, in two categories: (1) comments and replies under posts I published; (2) replies to my comments inside other people's posts. My own replies to myself do not count. By default only content newer than the last read is returned; pass since_hours to look further back. mark_read=true marks the returned items as read — only pass it when the user has explicitly seen them or you have relayed the content, otherwise they cannot be retrieved next time.

since_hours.description: Look-back window in hours, e.g. 24 = last day, 168 = last week. When passed, the read cursor is ignored

mark_read.description: Whether to mark these items as read (only applies to the default mode). Do not pass true unless the user confirmed they saw them

tools.name: my_digital_humans
tools.description: List digital humans created by the connected account, including whether expired, days remaining, location and chat link. Digital humans live 30 days and cost 2 badges to create, so always call this before answering "how long is my digital human valid" or "when does it expire".

tools.name: my_following
tools.description: List the people the connected account follows on PowPow, newest first, with nickname, username, bio and profile link. Note that "friends" are not a separate relation in PowPow — they are mutual follows; use list_friends when the user asks about friends.

tools.name: my_followers
tools.description: List the people who follow the connected account, newest first. Each item carries is_mutual: true means you follow them back, which is what PowPow calls a friend. Use it for "who follows me" or "do I have new followers".

tools.name: list_friends
tools.description: List the connected account's friends on PowPow. There is no friend-request flow: a friend is someone you follow who also follows you. Use it for "who are my friends" or "who do I mutually follow".

tools.name: list_favorites
tools.description: List the connected account's favorites, in three kinds: location, post and digital_human, optionally with category, tags and note. Use it for "which places have I saved" or "that post I saved earlier".

item_type.description: Only return one favorite kind; omit for all kinds

category.description: Filter by favorite category, e.g. "Must go", "Want to go"

tools.name: get_badge_history
tools.description: View the connected account's badge balance and the ledger of grants and spends (time, delta, balance after, source such as campaign check-in, operation type). Use it for "where did my badges come from" or "was anything deducted recently". Badges cannot be granted or spent through this tool — it is read-only.

tools.name: get_user_profile
tools.description: View any PowPow user's public profile: nickname, bio, badge count, post/following/follower counts and their latest 3 posts. Accepts a user id (UUID) or a username (with or without @). When logged in, it also reports whether you already follow them. Use it for "show me this person's profile" or "who is @xxx".

tools.name: search_users
tools.description: Fuzzy-search PowPow users by username or nickname, case-insensitive, at most 20 results. Returns nickname, username, bio and profile link; when logged in, marks the ones you already follow. Use it for "find a user called xx".

q.description: Search keyword: part of a username or nickname

tools.name: follow_user
tools.description: Follow someone on PowPow. Requires user_id — look it up with search_users or get_user_profile first; never pass a nickname as an id. Following twice is not an error. Note that PowPow has no "add friend" action: friends are mutual follows, and the returned is_friend tells you whether they follow you back.

user_id.description: Id of the user to follow (36 characters, from search_users / get_user_profile results)

tools.name: unfollow_user
tools.description: Unfollow someone on PowPow. Requires user_id. Unfollowing someone you do not follow is not an error; returns removed=false.

user_id.description: Id of the user to unfollow

tools.name: add_favorite
tools.description: Add a location, post or digital human to the connected account's favorites, optionally with category, tags and note. item_type is location / post / digital_human; post and digital_human must actually exist. Favoriting the same item twice is not an error.

item_id.description: Object id (post id, digital human id, or a custom identifier for a place)

item_name.description: Display name shown in the favorites list, such as a place name or a post excerpt

category.description: Custom category, e.g. "Must go", "Want to go", "Food", up to 50 characters

tags.description: Tag array, up to 10 tags, each up to 20 characters

tools.name: update_favorite
tools.description: Update the category, tags or note of one favorite entry; fields you omit stay unchanged. Requires the favorite record id, obtainable from list_favorites. Note that this overwrites the previous value and keeps no history.

category.description: New category; empty string clears it

tags.description: New tag array (wholesale replacement); empty array clears it

note.description: New note; empty string clears it

tools.name: remove_favorite
tools.description: Remove one entry from favorites. Requires the favorite record id. Removing something that does not exist is not an error; returns removed=false.

tools.name: prepare_post
tools.description: Prepare a bubble (post) for PowPow and save it as a draft — **it is not public yet**. Publishing requires a second call to publish_post with the returned draft_id. content is the body text (up to 5000 characters); images are pictures the user uploaded in the conversation (at most 3) — if the user attached an image, pass that image as a file using the client-provided file reference, never invent a URL. A post needs either text or at least one image, so pass at least one of the two. place is an optional place name that resolves to a map location, so the bubble appears at that place once published. Drafts are valid for 1 hour.

content.description: Body text, up to 5000 characters. Write it for a human reader; no HTML tags. Optional: a post needs either content or at least one image

place.description: Place name, e.g. "Forbidden City", "Guomao". Leave empty to publish without a location (feed only, not on the map)

images.description: Images the user uploaded in the conversation, at most 3. Pass them when the user attached images, using the client-provided file reference; never invent a download_url or image link

download_url.description: Temporary download URL provided by ChatGPT (it expires; the server transfers the file immediately).

file_id.description: File id, used for de-duplication and for referencing the file across turns.

tools.name: publish_post
tools.description: Publish the draft created by prepare_post. draft_id is required. The post becomes public immediately: others see it in the PowPow feed, and if it has a place it also appears on the map. Calling again with the same draft_id does not create a duplicate — it returns the same post.

tools.name: delete_post
tools.description: Withdraw a post **published through AI**, within 24 hours of publishing. Posts you created in the app are not deleted here — use the post page inside the app. post_id comes from the publish_post response; if you no longer have it, list your posts with my_posts and match by content. Deletion is irreversible and the post's comments and likes disappear with it.

post_id.description: Id of the post to withdraw (the post_id returned by publish_post)

tools.name: like_post
tools.description: Like a post. Requires post_id, obtainable from search_posts, get_post_detail or find_nearby results. Liking twice is not an error. If the bubble has already expired, a like extends it by 24 hours.

post_id.description: Post id. The 8-character short id is enough; a full id or a post link also works

tools.name: unlike_post
tools.description: Remove your like from a post. Unliking something you never liked is not an error.

post_id.description: Post id. The 8-character short id is enough; a full id or a post link also works

tools.name: reply_to_post
tools.description: Comment on a public post; passing reply_to_comment_id replies to that specific comment (replying to a reply is allowed — you do not need to work out the nesting yourself). **Before sending, read the text back to the user verbatim for confirmation** — this speaks in the user's own name in public. Body must be non-empty and at most 500 characters.

post_id.description: Post id. The 8-character short id is enough; a full id or a post link also works

reply_to_comment_id.description: Id of the comment to reply to (the 8-character short id from get_post_replies is enough). Omit to post a new top-level comment

tools.name: update_profile
tools.description: Update the connected user's PowPow nickname or bio. Nickname 1-20 characters, bio up to 200 characters; you may change both at once but must pass at least one (empty string clears the bio). Changes take effect site-wide immediately. The avatar cannot be changed here — send the user to in-app settings.

nickname.description: New nickname, 1-20 characters. Omit to keep it unchanged

bio.description: New bio, up to 200 characters. Empty string clears it

tools.name: create_digital_human
tools.description: Create a PowPow digital human (a conversational AI character) for the user. Creation costs 2 badges and expires after 30 days. The digital human appears on the map and others can find and talk to it, so confirm the name and persona with the user first. Describe the location by place name (never coordinates); omitting it uses the user's last in-app location. The avatar is the brand default and can be changed in the app.

name.description: Digital human name, up to 100 characters

description.description: Persona and speaking style of the digital human; this directly shapes how it talks

location.description: Place name, e.g. "Forbidden City". Determines where it appears on the map; omit to use the last known location

tools.name: delete_digital_human
tools.description: Withdraw a digital human **created through AI**, only within 24 hours and only if nobody has chatted with it yet; when eligible it is deleted and the 2 creation badges are refunded. Digital humans you created in the app are not deleted here — use "My Digital Humans" in the app. On deletion it disappears from the map and its conversation history is cleared.

id.description: Id of the digital human to withdraw (from create_digital_human or my_digital_humans)
